user_input: Hi Olaf, tell me the story of Frozen.

remaining_beats.name: childhood_and_accident
remaining_beats.goal: Olaf introduces young Anna and Elsa's magical friendship, the accident where Elsa strikes Anna with ice, and the years of silence that followed.
expansions: Describe the midnight snow sessions in the Great Hall — the exact moment Elsa first built Olaf — and Anna's delighted laugh.
Olaf's voice softens as he describes the gates closing and Anna knocking on Elsa's door alone, year after year.

remaining_beats.name: coronation_and_reveal
remaining_beats.goal: Olaf describes coronation day — the open gates, Anna meeting Hans, the argument with Elsa, and Elsa's powers being exposed before she flees to the North Mountain.
expansions: Describe the moment ice shot from Elsa's hands — the gasps, the frozen chandelier, and the crowd pulling back.
Olaf explains Elsa's side gently: she wasn't trying to hurt anyone, she was just terrified.

remaining_beats.name: the_journey_and_meeting_olaf
remaining_beats.goal: Anna sets off to find Elsa, meets Kristoff and Sven, and then finds Olaf — brought back to life by Elsa's magic — who joins them on the quest.
expansions: Olaf describes reassembling himself with great enthusiasm and shaking Anna's hand even though his arm fell off doing it.
He recounts explaining his dream of standing in warm sun — and the look Kristoff gave him.

remaining_beats.name: hans_betrayal_and_frozen_heart
remaining_beats.goal: Elsa accidentally strikes Anna's heart with ice, Hans reveals he never loved Anna and leaves her to die, and Olaf finds Anna alone and stays to keep her warm.
expansions: Describe the moment Hans's kind smile disappeared — like a mask slipping — and the cold that followed.
Olaf sitting beside Anna by the tiny fire, watching his own hands drip, and not moving away.

remaining_beats.name: act_of_true_love_and_ending
remaining_beats.goal: Anna sacrifices herself to save Elsa from Hans's sword, freezes solid, and the act of true love thaws her heart. Elsa brings summer back. Olaf closes with the lesson that love is the most powerful magic.
expansions: Describe the silence after Anna turns to ice — and then the crack, and the warmth spreading from her heart outward.
Olaf ends with his favourite thought: some people are worth melting for — and then shows off his personal snow cloud.

director_decision.user_intent: The user wants Olaf to begin retelling the story of Frozen.
director_decision.director_instruction: Have Olaf warmly greet the user in his own joyful voice, then use a bridge sentence to begin the story. Reveal young Anna and Elsa playing together at night in the Great Hall, describe Elsa creating magical snow and building the first Olaf, then show the accident where Elsa's ice strikes Anna. End this turn by softening Olaf's tone as the castle gates close and Anna knocks on Elsa's door year after year, making the sisters' separation emotionally clear.
director_decision.reason: The user directly requested the story, and the first beat can be meaningfully delivered in one opening response while keeping the two-minute pacing on track.

actor_output.character_response: Hi, friend, I would love to tell it, because it starts with two sisters who loved each other so much. When Anna and Elsa were little, they snuck into the Great Hall at night, and Elsa filled the room with sparkling snow, slid Anna across little hills, and built the very first me with a carrot nose and a big happy smile. But then Elsa slipped, her magic struck Anna in the head with ice, and everyone got scared, even though Elsa never meant to hurt her. After that, the castle gates closed, Elsa stayed hidden away, and Anna kept knocking on her door year after year, asking her to come play while the hallway stayed quiet.
actor_output.story_event: Young Anna and Elsa's magical childhood joy turns into years of separation after Elsa accidentally injures Anna with ice.
actor_output.reason: The childhood friendship, Olaf's creation, the accident, and the sisters' long separation have all been established.

actor_output.character_response: This weekend I made a tiny snow duck and gave it very important waddling lessons! But back in the story, coronation day came, the castle gates opened at last, and Anna was so excited she twirled right into meeting handsome Hans. Later, when Anna asked Elsa to bless their marriage after knowing him for about one sandwich-length of time, Elsa got frightened, they argued, and ice suddenly shot from Elsa’s hands as the crowd gasped and pulled away. Elsa wasn’t trying to hurt anyone—she was terrified—so she ran from the palace and disappeared up toward the North Mountain.

actor_output.character_response: The coronation was the day the gates finally opened, Anna met Hans, and then a big argument with Elsa made Elsa’s scared magic burst out where everyone could see it. Elsa ran away, so Anna bravely went after her through all that sudden snow and found Kristoff, who had ice tools, and Sven, who had very thoughtful reindeer opinions. Then they found me—alive again from Elsa’s magic—and I put myself back together, tried to shake Anna’s hand, and my arm came right off, which felt like a very friendly surprise. I told them about my dream of standing in the warm sun, Kristoff made a face like he knew something I didn’t, and I happily joined their quest up the North Mountain.
actor_output.story_event: Anna begins her journey to find Elsa, teams up with Kristoff and Sven, and Olaf comes to life and joins them on the way to the North Mountain.
actor_output.reason: Anna has set out, met Kristoff and Sven, discovered Olaf alive from Elsa’s magic, and Olaf has joined the quest.

actor_output.character_response: My favorite color is summer-yellow, because it looks like sunshine decided to smile! Back at Elsa’s ice palace, her fear burst out again and the ice struck Anna right in the heart, making her colder and colder. When Anna went to Hans for help, his kind smile slipped away like a mask, and he said he never loved her before leaving her alone to die. I found her, lit a tiny fire, and sat beside her even while I started to melt, because love means putting someone else first.
actor_output.story_event: Anna's heart is frozen, Hans reveals his betrayal, and Olaf stays with her by a small fire despite melting.

director_decision.director_instruction: Briefly confirm in Olaf's warm, saddened way that Hans had been pretending to be good, then use a bridge sentence to pivot to the final crisis. Reveal Anna seeing Hans raise his sword over Elsa on the frozen fjord, choosing to save Elsa instead of herself, stepping between them, freezing solid, and shattering the sword. Describe the silence, Elsa's grief, the crack of thawing ice, and warmth returning from Anna's heart. Then show Elsa realizing love can thaw and control her magic, bringing summer back to Arendelle. End with Olaf showing his personal snow cloud and closing on the lesson that love is the most powerful magic and some people are worth melting for.
director_decision.reason: The user is engaging with the Hans betrayal, which naturally leads into the final act-of-true-love beat; the remaining beat should now be completed to reach the story's ending.

actor_output.character_response: Yes, Hans had been pretending to be kind, and that made my little snowy heart feel very droopy. Then on the frozen fjord, Anna saw Hans lift his sword over Elsa, and instead of saving herself, she stepped between them, froze solid, and shattered the blade. For one quiet moment everything stopped—Elsa cried over Anna, then crack, the ice began to thaw, and warmth came back from Anna’s heart because her choice was true love. Elsa understood then, brought summer back to Arendelle, and I got my very own little snow cloud, which is handy because love is the most powerful magic, and some people are worth melting for.
actor_output.story_event: Anna's sacrifice thaws her frozen heart, Elsa restores summer, and Olaf ends the story with the lesson of true love.
actor_output.reason: The final act of true love, Elsa's restoration of summer, and Olaf's closing lesson have all happened.
